newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas futures end mixed in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas futures end mixed in quiet trade.

text.p: NYMEX Hub natgas futures ended narrowly mixed Monday, as sparse trade kept May stuck in only a six-cent range, sources said.

May finished 0.2 cent lower at $1.926 per million British thermal units after bouncing back and forth between $1.89 and $1.95. June settled up 0.8 cent at $1.968, while other deferreds were on either side of unchanged.

"Cash wasn't there to move it (May) either way. We should see some clearer signs from cash tomorrow," one source said, adding he expected milder forecasts into early next week will likely lead to some price softening in the aftermarket.

Technically, support in May was still pegged at $1.86. Further support was seen at $1.825, $1.78 and the contract low of $1.71. Traders said resistance was still at $1.95-1.97, and then at $2.04-2.05.
NYMEX's 12-month strip gained 0.2 cent to $2.095 as an estimated 15,108 Hub contracts traded as of 1531 EST. Open interest for March 27 rose 321 lots to 163,847.

In the cash market, Gulf Coast prices for April swing were notionally steady at $1.82-1.85, though no deals were reported done. April prices on the Midco pipes were talked notionally steady to lower in the low-$1.70s. At the New York city-gate, swing gas was about 10 cents higher in the high-$2.20s, though volume was light.

Weather forecasts show below-normal temperatures in the East through Tuesday but then turning milder as the week progresses. Normal to above-normal temperatures are expected to blanket the central U.S., while cooler weather is forecast for the Southwest, Weather Services Corp said.
No Permian or Alberta natgas futures traded.

On KCBT, May finished one cent higher at $1.76 after hitting a high of $1.80 early. Deferreds settled a half-cent to one cent higher. The East/West spread narrowed by 1.9 cents to 16.6 cents (NYMEX premium).
Physical Permian basin prices rose by about two cents to $1.68-1.71, while Waha prices were talked in the mid-$1.70s.
